models.experiment: A structured comparison of one or more interventions against a baseline, with a hypothesis, an outcome metric, a time-series of results, and a decision the city has reached (or has not yet reached).
models.experimentIntervention: A single intervention being compared inside an experiment. May be flagged as the baseline, which represents the 'do nothing different' control.
models.metric: The single metric the experiment is measured against (label and unit) — for example, 'Litter items per week'.
models.seriesPoint: One data point in an intervention's outcome series — a date label and a numeric value of the metric on that date.
models.outcomeSeries: Per-intervention time series of metric values aligned to the same date axis. Each series is keyed to an interventionId from the experiment's interventions list.
models.decision: The city's verdict on the experiment, the rationale behind it, and the recommended next action. May be undecided for experiments still running.

relationships: An experiment has many interventions; exactly one of them is the baseline (or none, for planned experiments not yet structured).
An experiment has one metric and one outcomeSeries.
outcomeSeries has one entry per interventionId in the experiment's interventions list.
An experiment has zero or one decision — concluded experiments have one, running and planned experiments may have none.

experiments.title: Painted footprints to the bins
experiments.hypothesis: Bright lime footprints leading from the busiest seating area to the nearest bins will increase disposal rates and reduce litter accumulation in the south plaza.
experiments.summary: Six-week field test against a no-paint baseline period (Mar 1 – Apr 14). Metric measured weekly across the south plaza only.

interventions.name: Baseline (no paint)
interventions.description: Pre-intervention period with the square in its previous state. Used as the control reference.

interventions.name: Painted footprints
interventions.description: Bright lime footprints painted on the pavement from the south seating area to the nearest two waste bins.

experiments.title: Cigarette voting ashtrays
experiments.hypothesis: Transparent ashtrays posing a weekly question, where visitors vote with their butts, will increase ashtray disposal and reduce ground butts at the south entrance.
experiments.summary: Two ashtrays at the south entrance, weekly question rotation. Metric is butts collected from the ground in the south entrance zone.

interventions.name: Baseline (standard ashtrays)
interventions.description: Pre-intervention period with conventional ashtrays at the south entrance.

interventions.name: Voting ashtrays
interventions.description: Transparent voting ashtrays with rotating weekly question, replacing the conventional pair.

experiments.title: Signage rewrite at north gate
experiments.hypothesis: Replacing the prohibitive 'no littering' sign with a humorous, gratitude-framed message will reduce litter in the north entrance area.
experiments.summary: Eight-week test comparing the new sign against a six-week pre-intervention baseline. The new sign yielded a small but consistent reduction.

interventions.name: Baseline (old sign)
interventions.description: Original 'no littering — fine €50' sign in place.

interventions.name: Gratitude sign
interventions.description: Illustrated sign thanking visitors for keeping the square living and clean.

decision.rationale: Consistent ~15% reduction across eight weeks with no observed downsides. Effect is modest but durable, and the sign is essentially zero-cost to maintain.
decision.action: Roll the gratitude sign template out to the south and east entrances in Q3.

experiments.title: Extra bins at night
experiments.hypothesis: Adding two temporary bins near the south seating area between 18:00 and 02:00 will reduce after-hours litter accumulation.
experiments.summary: Ten-week test. Bins were used heavily but did not produce a statistically meaningful reduction in ground litter; cleaning crew reported the bins overflowed twice on weekends.

interventions.name: Baseline (no extra bins)
interventions.description: Existing bin layout as configured before the test.

interventions.name: Extra night bins
interventions.description: Two temporary bins placed near the south seating area, present 18:00–02:00.

decision.rationale: No meaningful reduction in litter, plus operational burden from overflow. Bins are heavily used but appear to displace rather than capture additional waste.
decision.action: Remove the temporary bins. Reroute the resources into the painted-footprints test in Q2.

experiments.title: Summer evening cleaning shift
experiments.hypothesis: Extending Friday and Saturday cleaning to 22:00 during the summer high-traffic season will reduce Saturday- and Sunday-morning litter visible to early visitors.
experiments.summary: Three-month pilot scheduled to start June 1. Metric will be Saturday/Sunday 8:00 ground-litter count.

interventions.name: Baseline (current schedule)
interventions.description: Current cleaning schedule ending at 19:00 on Friday and Saturday.

interventions.name: Late-evening cleaning
interventions.description: Extend Friday and Saturday cleaning to 22:00 throughout June, July, and August.

experiments.title: Saturday citizen sweep ritual
experiments.hypothesis: A volunteer-led 30-minute sweep every Saturday at 9:00, anchored by a coffee reward at the corner café, will create visible weekly cleanliness improvements and shift visitor attitudes toward the square as cared-for.
experiments.summary: Twelve-week pilot. Two metrics: ground-litter count Saturday 9:30 vs. 9:00, and a short post-sweep visitor sentiment intercept.

interventions.name: Baseline (no organized sweep)
interventions.description: Saturdays as currently observed, with no organized volunteer activity.

interventions.name: Saturday citizen sweep
interventions.description: Weekly 30-minute volunteer-led sweep starting at 9:00, with coffee reward at the partnering café.
